subject: Very slow sampling for heirarchical multivariate continuous time / stochastic differential model

messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: Very slow sampling for heirarchical multivariate continuous time / stochastic differential model
parts:
I've done up an R function to estimate continuous time panel / time series models (as per https://cran.rstudio.com/web/packages/ctsem/index.html) in a heirarchical fashion. I've cholesky'd and vectorized and noncentered everything I could, but am finding sampling very slow, and would really appreciate some feedback on the model, if anyone has some thoughts. There's a fair bit going on, so to try and explain:

nmanifest observed variables Y are observed at multiple time points for each of nsubjects and arranged into an ndatapoints array of vectors of nmanifest length.

each of the ndatapoints Y vectors is distributed according to some intercept vector MANIFESTMEANS, a latent vector eta multiplied by a loading matrix LAMBDA (though here simply diagonal 1's), and some measurement noise, MANIFESTVARchol.

Each of the ndatapoints latent vectors eta (except the first for each subject) is a function of an intercept, discreteCINT, the earlier vector eta(t-1) multiplied by discreteDRIFT, and some sampled perturbation vector (latentError) multiplied by discreteDIFFUSIONchol. All discretePARAMS are in turn a function of dT (the length of time between observations), and continuous time parameter matrices CINT, DRIFT, DIFFUSIONchol.

The continuous time parameter matrices are (when necessary) recovered from transformed versions (e.g. DRIFTlog) that allow unbounded estimation.

These transformed continuous time parameters are stacked into: vector[nparams] indparams[nsubjects]

each row of indparams (each subjects parameters) is then a function of a hypermeans vector + diag_pre_multiply(hypersd,hypercorrchol) multiplied by random vector indparamsnoise[subjecti]

The model, script and data to run via R are attached. Some chains with a few hundred iterations can be found here:
https://www.dropbox.com/s/3fjs8k4vrqks9ln/example_ctStanFit11.rda?dl=0

Is there some way to vectorize sampling for imputedY (I realise the imputation is not appropriate, but have no missing Y in this data anyway) that I am missing (given that MANIFESTVARchol is not always a diagonal matrix) ?

I'm not totally sure how to diagnose the problems here, and would be very happy for any general guidance / links that might be appropriate... I know that sampling is much faster in some chains than for others, though in general seems slow. Am I expecting too much? It took a day or two to sample the above chains for a fairly small problem size - this clearly won't scale, though I'm eager to see how advi goes once it's in rstan.  There were a few divergent iterations, so I guess I also need a higher adapt delta, but that won't help speed.

Cheers for any help!
Charlie
